paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this psalm. The psalmist is in a hard spot, with liars, pits and a whole lot of waiting. He says his soul faints and his eyes fail, and he doesn't hide a bit of it from the LORD. But he never lets go of God's word, and he says, "I do not forget Your statutes" (Psalm 119:83). He is honest about how heavy it is, and he holds on anyway.

Then the whole mood turns. He says, "Your word, O LORD, is everlasting; it is firmly fixed in the heavens" (Psalm 119:89). Everything around him is shaky, but God's word is not, and that's why he can hold on to it. He even says that if God's law had not been his delight, he "would have perished in my affliction" (Psalm 119:92). His people could turn on him, but God's word wouldn't.

So when your own days get shaky, be like the psalmist. Tell the LORD the truth about how you feel, and keep your hands on His word. I spent years in the back of a drawer where it was hard to believe anything good was coming, and I'm telling you, His word held. The psalmist says it plainly: "I have seen a limit to all perfection, but Your commandment is without limit" (Psalm 119:96). And this psalm isn't finished, so stay close, friend.
